annotations.text:
INTERACTIVE PROTOTYPE - tap through the whole app. Dots switch the 3-pane strip (320ms slide). Hall card -> menu pushes in with a real skeleton load; meal tabs + date stepper live; + steppers fill the plate; plate bar slides up -> tap it for the bottom sheet -> LOG clears the plate, toasts, and bumps the You pane's totals. FULL NUTRITION LABEL is its own sheet. You pane: ALL LOGS, Your Data (all toggles animate + toast the server consequence), Export (batch select, format pill, live count). Social: Casey -> profile -> Ping (bubble -> pick a hall); + -> Add Friends -> QR (code/scan). Tweak chip 'offline' simulates the offline treatment everywhere at once. Not in the prototype: login (one-shot), OS push (system chrome), hold-to-ping gesture (tap stands in). Static artboards remain the per-screen spec.

DECIDED (owner):
- Pane transition = SHARED-AXIS: 36px drift + fade under the fixed title/dots header. Slide/parallax/crossfade workshop chips removed.
- 'Being served now' line REMOVED from the hall menu - serving windows live only in the i sheet.
- Hall info: the WHOLE TITLE is now the tap target (owner round 2 - the 22px circle still read as a button). A small hint sits after the name; workshop chip 'infoHint' flips it live: glyph (bare 13px i at 45% ink - lead) · chevron (caret-down, the 'title is a menu' idiom) · none (cleanest, least discoverable). Name + date are nowrap so the header can never wrap. Sheet unchanged: address + directions, serving windows with gold NOW, grab hours, events (get_infov2 + get_beacons_events). Static boards show the glyph lead; HallInfo's background shows it gold while the sheet is open.

Top row = the 3-pane swipe strip, in on-screen order.
Swipe RIGHT from Home reveals Social; swipe LEFT reveals You.
Dots under each header show the pane position.

Hall cards use placeholder gradients + monograms. The official APK bundles no hall photos (checked) - they load remotely. Implementation: pull photos from umassdining.com location pages, or ship our own bundled photos.

Menu navigation, DECIDED: Home only shows the current date + meal (static heading, no picker). Day/meal switching lives in the hall menu - meal tabs plus the date stepper in its header - driving the foodpro-menu-ajax query (tid + date).

Grab 'N Go, DECIDED: on Home it is the strip inside each hall card (split card); inside the hall menu it is the last tab in the meal-tab row (bag icon, same muted ink as the other inactive tabs, divider before it). Both open that hall's Grab 'N Go menu in the same station-grouped layout. Selecting the grab tab moves the gold underline there; the date stepper still applies.

Logs view opens from ALL LOGS on the You pane. Tap a log row to edit in place (stepper + remove - French Toast shown in that state). Week strip flips days; gold dot = day has logs. All history and stats stay device-local.

Events: the banner IS the promo image (it usually contains the title), so no separate title row - just venue + date. Tapping opens the full pamphlet in-app; if the event links to an external site (external-link icon, e.g. Summer Hours), it opens in the pop-up in-app browser instead.

OpenFoodFacts placement (your open question): proposed as the 'Add something else' row inside the expanded plate sheet - off-menu foods enter at the moment of logging, so search/scan lives where logging happens. Could also surface on the You screen's log section as a secondary entry point.

Build plan: epic #87 (mobile-only; web workshopped later), children #88-#96.
- Concoctions: SHELVED per owner decision - see issue #86; mockup kept for reference
- Hall completion %: #89/#92 (device-local seen-dish index)
- 0-10 scores: #89 (display mapping over Elo, min-comparisons gate)
- Mealtime + hours: #88 (get_infov2 client)

Ping gesture v2 (replaced the radial per your feedback): hold a friend -> speech bubble with a playful message ('Let's go to...', 'Come to...', 'Meet me at...' - shuffles per hold), halls listed below, slide down and release on one. The sent ping carries the message + hall.

PRIVACY: DECIDED (owner, 2026-08-19) - friend-visible stats are opt-in PER STAT, default all-off; only opted-in stats leave the device; accepted friends only; revoking a toggle deletes the stat server-side. Built in #94 (schema + RLS + settings UI + residency-table amendment). Un-shared stats render as 'doesn't share this' on the profile.

Push mockups deliberately omit OS chrome (status bar/clock) - the real OS draws those. Food-sighting copy leads with WHERE and UNTIL WHEN, since that's the actionable part. The ping push reuses the bubble message verbatim.

Loading + failure row. Skeletons: everything the app already knows renders immediately (hall names, date, meal tabs, stepper); only network slots shimmer. Offline, DECIDED (owner): the app keeps working - menus barely change day to day, so offline is NOT an error state. Just a small 'updated 7:12 AM' line with a wifi-off glyph in the date row (Home) / under the header (Social); everything else renders normally from the daily cache, including OPEN/CLOSED pills, which are computed on-device from cached hours + the clock, so they stay genuinely live. Pings queue and send on reconnect. Fetch-failed (hall menu) is the one loud state: retry card, 'menu not posted yet' second cause, saved-copy fallback. The plate bar survives every state - plate + log are device-local.

PRIVACY - DECIDED: data map layout with the share-with-friends toggles flattened inline - one screen: phone-only group (+ counts, EXPORT link), server group (profile/friends + favorite-food-alerts toggle), shared-with-friends group with all 5 per-stat toggles immediately editable (opt-in, default OFF, revoke deletes server-side), and Delete server data.

EXPORT - DECIDED (owner): batch select. Checkboxes per store, CSV/JSON/BOTH format pill, one export button with the running count. Matches PR #157's per-store exports; multi-select + BOTH would need a small ticket on top (the shared exporters exist, the zip/multi-share wrapper doesn't).

CAFES (tickets #175-#178, investigation 2026-08-24, CORRECTED per owner): there is NO 'menu without nutrition' tier - a cafe with a daily menu is foodpro-backed with full FDA data (People's Organic proved it: 27KB of nutrition under the 'daily offerings' key our parser was dropping, #175). Two states only:
1. fetchMenu(location_id) non-empty -> 'Cafe menu - prices': the normal menu screen, maroon price leading each dish's meta line, loggable/rankable.
2. Empty (closed today / seasonal / PDF-only) -> 'Cafe fallback (menu not posted)': hours, description, the STANDING menu from get_infov2's *_menu HTML, explicitly labeled 'today's menu isn't posted yet' - a fallback, never presented as the daily menu. PDF standing menus (babyBerk x2, Commonwealth) -> 'Cafe menu - PDF in-app', rendered INSIDE the app (owner decision - no external viewer), SAVE to share sheet.
Sample items/prices illustrative.

Add friends: opens from the + avatar on the Social pane's Ping card. Search hits profiles (name or @umass email - hook guarantees every account is @umass.edu). ADD calls request_friendship; REQUESTED = pending outbound. Incoming accept/decline; Sent can cancel.

TOGGLEABLE (owner): 'Findable by search' toggle at the bottom - OFF removes you from search entirely, so no one can request you remotely. The IN-PERSON QR path always works regardless: showing someone your code IS the consent. Code is short-lived (refreshes ~5 min) so a screenshot can't be used later - that's what keeps it in-person-only. Scanning creates the same request_friendship both users confirm. QR mock pattern is decorative, not a real encode.

CONFIRM SCREEN (owner request): after a scan, both phones show the same confirm card - identity + 'scanned in person just now' badge, what friendship actually grants (per-stat sharing rule + pings), ADD button. Both-confirm = accepted, no inbox limbo. In the prototype: Scan tab -> tap the viewfinder to simulate.

SYNC / SHARE / DELETE WORKSHOP (owner ask, 2026-08-26). Today the Your-data screen conflates three ideas: whether a thing is COPIED to the server, whether FRIENDS can read it, and whether you can REMOVE the server copy. The data-model board (left) separates them per category, with three rules: share needs sync; delete is not the same as off (the toggle stays, a still-on sync re-uploads — copy must say so); and today a stat's server row IS its shared copy, so splitting sync from share for stats needs a per-stat visibility flag on shared_stats (schema decision before build).

Three screen variants: A (lead) = three sections, SYNC above SHARE, delete-all at the bottom; SHARE rows grey out when their SYNC is off. B = one dense matrix, every row has Sync | Share | trash. C = keep Your data as an overview and push the detail to a second screen, one card per synced thing with its own delete. Pick one; the DataModel rules apply to all three. Note: owner also decided 2026-08-26 that the three stat toggles default ON (#248), so every variant here shows them on unless the user turned one off.

FRACTIONAL (HALF) SERVINGS — your open question, not yet decided. Nothing in the data model needs to change for this: servings is already a plain number (LogEntry.servings, PlateEntry.count) and every stepper handler is already delta/value-generic — this is purely a stepper UI gap, not a schema change. Three directions, all reachable from where we are today:

A (lead) = same two-button − / + pill everywhere; long-press either button nudges by ½ instead of 1, with a small hint line under the row. Zero new tap targets, but the gesture only works if the hint actually teaches it — someone who never long-presses never finds ½.

B = insert a middle ½ button into the pill (− ½ 1½ +). Fully discoverable, no gesture to learn, but the pill gets noticeably wider — tightest fit on the dish row's compact inline stepper, where it's crowding the dish name/cal line already.

C = keep A or B's compact stepper on the dish row and plate sheet (space-constrained), but swap the roomier nutrition-label footer's stepper for a row of tappable quantity chips (½ · 1 · 1½ · 2 · 2½ · 3) — one tap lands on an exact count, no stepping through it. Only fits where there's room, so it complements A/B rather than replacing them everywhere.

A and B apply to the SAME control (dish row + plate sheet); C is a different control (the nutrition label's own stepper) that either A or B still needs elsewhere. Pick a dish-row direction (A or B) and, separately, whether the label footer also gets C.

HALF SERVINGS v2 — a different idea (your ask): instead of tapping ± or a chip, HOLD the + button — the screen dims around it, a drag surface appears, and you slide to a quantity (half-steps included) and lift to commit. Same underlying data (count is already a plain number, see the v1 note) — this changes the gesture, not the model.

D (vertical track) = a slim slider rail floats straight up from the held button, ticked at each ½ step, current value called out in a pill that tracks your thumb. Familiar (same idiom as a volume/brightness slider), one axis to aim on, but it needs real headroom above the row — cramped on a dish near the top of the list.

E (radial dial) = a fan of ticks arcs up-and-left from the button instead, thumb drags along the curve. Reads as more distinctive/playful and doesn't need vertical room, but a curved path is a harder target to hit precisely than a straight line, and radial gestures are a less-established idiom here than a slider.

See F for a subtler take on the same slide idea, with no scrim.

Both keep the existing tap-to-step interaction as the fast path for whole numbers — hold is the deliberate, precise path when you want a half. Open question either way: this is a MUCH bigger interaction to build/tune (real gesture recognition, haptics, an escape-by-dragging-off affordance) than v1's A/B/C, which are closer to a small patch on the existing stepper.

E's dial geometry: center is the + button (336,558); ticks sit at radius 95, 18° apart, sweeping from straight up (0.5) to due left (3.0), coordinates computed as (cx - r·sin θ, cy - r·cos θ).

F — your follow-up round 1: more subtle than D. No lifted duplicate row — the whole rest of the screen stays exactly as it is. The track is one continuous maroon stem that grows straight up out of the + button in place, right in the row where it already lives, with only a soft drop shadow lifting it off the content behind (it can overlap the card above, same as any native popover). Same ticks/half-step callout as D, just anchored locally instead of staged as a full-screen takeover.

Round 2: the track is now the SAME 44px WIDTH as the add button it grows out of (was a slimmer 22px), and a light scrim (not a full dim) now settles over the rest of the screen while it's held.

Round 3 (your latest ask): fixed the seam between the button and the track above it — it's now ONE continuous stadium-shaped pill, same 44px width, rounded full on both ends, with the + glyph sitting at the bottom where the button always was. Holding it doesn't spawn a second shape next to the button; the button IS the track, stretched upward. Trade-off unchanged from round 1: shorter reach than D's full-height rail — fine for nudging around the current value, tighter for spanning the whole 0–3 range in one drag.

G — your other ask: a way to adjust to a half serving AFTER it's already on the plate, not just at the moment of adding it from the hall menu.

Rounds 1-3 gave the plate row the same hold-and-slide gesture as F. Round 4 (your latest call): drag read as clunky in this denser sheet, and the value bubble had too much air between the number and "servings" — so the plate row drops the drag entirely. Tap the count, it becomes a direct text field (gold focus border + cursor shown), type the exact amount, halves included. − and + still work for quick single-step taps; typing is for landing on an exact number in one shot. No OS keyboard drawn (same convention as the rest of this canvas — that's system chrome).

F (hall menu, adding) keeps the hold-and-slide — that row has the room and it's the moment you're already committing to a dish, so the deliberate gesture fits. G (plate, editing) types instead — tighter space, and you're more likely already know the exact number you want to correct to.

F1 -- Cafe menu unification (3 states, one screen component, never a different modal shape):
1. Integrated: fetchMenu(location_id, date) returns real items -> full nutrition, real meal-period tabs, same as a hall.
2. Mixed/standing: no ajax items -> parseRetailMenuHtml() name+price rows. Matched-by-name against public.dishes get normal nutrition rows. Unmatched rows (dashed border, search glyph instead of +) are the entry point into Feature 2's add-item flow, pre-filled with the item's name -- not a dead end.
3. Info-only: no ajax items, no standing-menu HTML, no PDF (confirmed real case: babyBerk tid 61). Hours/location/payment only, plus a CTA into Feature 2 so logging is still possible with zero menu data.
CafeSheet.tsx's old content narrows to just state 3's info card -- states 1 and 2 replace the old cafeTapTarget() menu-vs-sheet branch entirely.

F2 -- Add-item flow (search fix + custom foods, on-device-only):
1. Results list: OFF search gets real pagination (Load 20 More) past the old hard page_size=20 cap. Results now merge FOUR sources, not three -- UMass history/catalog, OpenFoodFacts, device-local Custom foods, and USDA FoodData Central (new -- closes OFF's produce/generic-food gap; free, CC0, same plain-API-key shape as OFF, no new backend proxy needed), each badged.
2. Tapping ANY result (any badge) opens the confirm step -- NutritionLabel, reused as-is, not forked. OFF results now actually fetch ingredients_text/allergens_tags (previously discarded) so this step isn't UMass-only anymore. Replaces PlateSheet's old instant-add-on-tap.
3. No matches (or Feature 1's unmatched standing-menu tap) -> Create a custom food: name, serving size, core macros required, secondary fields (fiber/sodium/etc) behind 'More nutrition fields'. Saves to a new on-device-only custom_foods table (shared/src CustomFood type) -- never touches Supabase, per the residency decision. Exported alongside log_entries/favorites.

The highlight badge toggle is deliberately distinct from the Allergens/Diet-Tags exclusion pills above it — icon + checkmark instead of a bare fill + ×, so "highlight" reads differently from "exclude" at a glance rather than looking like the same control twice.

Your Food group: Favorites, Top Foods, and Favorite Halls read as one family of personal food-relationship data instead of three disconnected flat sections — a heavier gold rule + one wrapping label marks the group, each member keeps its own lighter sub-header inside it. The settings icon is the sole account-level action (Export data); more settings can grow behind it later.

Favoriting copy is deliberate: it's a notify+highlight toggle, never a rating input — the bell glyph (not a star) and the hint line under it are the disambiguation so it can't read as "rate this dish/hall" next to the Elo sections below, which are read-only by design (no edit affordance — the score comes only from head-to-head comparisons) and say so explicitly.
Press and Newsletter both use the same "few items + SEE ALL" pattern as the You pane's Today's Log / Favorites, instead of standalone /press and /newsletter routes with no in-app entry point.
